newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds dip after good start,US data in focus.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds dip after good start,US data in focus.

text.p: Danish bond prices fell slightly on Wednesday after getting off to a good start, with the market undertone good but subject to technical trading ahead of the afternoon's U.S. key data.
"Technical trading is affecting the market, but the general tone is good ahead of the American industrial, capacity and housing start figures," one dealer said.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down 0.23 point from the opening or 0.11 point up from Tuesday's close at 109.49, yielding 6.55 percent in turnover of 800 million crowns.
The 2006 benchmark's June future rose 0.44 point to 109.00 with 137 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 was unchanged at 87.73.
The crown traded at an unchanged 3.8080 per mark at 1130 gmt.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany widened one basis point to 72.
The Central Bank was active on the market selling a total of 905 million crowns worth of seven percent 2007 and six percent 2002 bonds as part of its routine financing operations.
